test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If sinB=(sqrt3)/(2), then find the value of (sqrt3 cosecB+secB-4)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: **sinB = √3/2** ⇒ **B = 60°**.

Put B = 60° in **√3 cosecB + secB − 4**.

⇒ √3 × (2/√3) + 2 − 4

⇒ 2 + 2 − 4 = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** sinB = √3/2

**Formula Used:** cosecB = 1/sinB; secB = 1/cosB; sin²B + cos²B = 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64db062619e30dbea57804b7dcab9699baa7f7529287ea9ba9599e257a911d4b.png] 

⇒ sinB = √3/2 ⇒ Perpendicular(P) = √3, Hypotenuse(H) = 2

⇒ Base(B) = √(H² − P²) = √(2² − (√3)²) = √(4 − 3) = 1

⇒ cosecB = H/P = 2/√3

⇒ secB = H/B = 2/1 = 2

⇒ Expression = (√3 × 2/√3) + 2 − 4

⇒ Expression = 2 + 2 − 4 = 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Table Values (60°)

sin60° = √3/2, cos60° = 1/2, tan60° = √3, cot60° = 1/√3, sec60° = 2, cosec60° = 2/√3.

Reciprocal Identities

sinθ = 1/cosecθ, cosθ = 1/secθ, tanθ = 1/cotθ.

Pythagorean Triplets

For a right-angled triangle, a² + b² = c². Standard triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (1, √3, 2).</p
